clue.text: Genuine article secured by relative, almost 100

indicators.note: the article is held fast within the relative, so one piece sits inside the other
almost means the relative's word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: an aunt or auntie is a relative
the definite article in English
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for an item being genuine because a relative of nearly a hundred has kept it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost 100' tempts you to trim the number, but 'almost' belongs to the relative, leaving AUNTI; 'secured by' wraps it round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic is real and not fake, which is what genuine means; the two are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Section of diagram is surely wrong

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a drawing is certainly mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is faulty or not as it should be, so it is wrong.

clue.text: Draw level, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the level word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a tier is a level, as in a tiered cake

explanation.surface: A short instruction to make a game end all square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw level' reads as one phrase, but 'Draw' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a drawn game, one in which neither side wins.

clue.text: Leap, then react unsteadily

indicators.note: unsteadily means wobbling, so the letters of these words lose their order

explanation.surface: Someone jumps and then lands with a wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet jump in which the dancer crosses the feet several times in the air.

clue.text: A doctor during excursion produces drum

indicators.note: the doctor sits within the excursion, inside it in time and so in letters

parts.note: a tour is an excursion
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor on an outing makes music on a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambour is a small drum, an old name for a tabor or side drum.

clue.text: Exclusive group from lake bed, originally

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A select circle that began on the bed of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lake bed' reads as one thing, but the bed comes first in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small, select clique of people sharing an interest.

clue.text: Mark's small vehicle

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A man called Mark owns a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is the definition; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Anger in vandalised crescent in Cotswolds town

indicators.note: the anger word is placed in the scrambled crescent, inside it
vandalised means smashed up, so the letters of the word crescent are rearranged

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Fury at a vandalised row of houses in a country town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' scrambles the crescent (CRENCEST) and 'in' places the anger after its C. The Cotswolds are a rural hill area in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cirencester is a market town in Gloucestershire, often called the capital of the Cotswolds.

clue.text: Tries in proper practice session

indicators.note: the tries word is placed in the proper word, inside it

parts.note: real means proper or genuine
to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: Rugby tries scored in a real training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like rugby; it is the legal sense, hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a run-through before the real performance, a practice session.

clue.text: Starts to dispute it, so-called course record

indicators.note: the starts of the words that follow, their first letters, are taken

explanation.surface: Someone begins to question a supposed course record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course record' reads as one phrase, but 'course' gives the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the vinyl kind played on a turntable.

clue.text: Splendid point female ignored, being silly

indicators.note: the female letter is ignored, so it is left out of the word for splendid

parts.note: fine means splendid or excellent

explanation.surface: A fine debating point is wasted because a woman was overlooked, which seems foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes the female from the word for splendid, leaving INE; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking sense, so a silly, foolish action can be called that.

clue.text: Feisty old woman's protest about limited hearing

indicators.note: the protest word goes around the shortened hearing, so one encloses the other

parts.note: a march is a protest by demonstrators

indicators.note: limited means the hearing word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A spirited old lady demonstrates because her court case was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' suggests the ears, but it is a court case; 'limited' clips its last letter and 'about' sets the protest around what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is the formidable female head of a family, a strong-minded elderly woman.

clue.text: Put on ring, gold, in players' entrance

parts.note: to stage a play is to put it on
the letter O is ring-shaped
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone stages a show with a golden ring at the actors' door.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors use the backstage door of a theatre to come and go, so it is the players' entrance.

clue.text: Bored, a nurse going round a Cornish resort carrying son

indicators.note: the nurse word goes round the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: to tend is to nurse

indicators.note: the resort carries the son within it, so it goes inside

parts.note: Looe is a seaside town in Cornwall, England

explanation.surface: A weary nurse makes the rounds of a Cornish seaside town with a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' slips the son into the resort, and 'going round' has the nurse word enclose the second a plus that result, two containers nested.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with nothing to do is idle, an idiom for being bored and unoccupied.

clue.text: Line dance?

parts.note: a cryptic reading: a dance performed by people moving in a single line, each holding the one in front

explanation.surface: A question about a dance done in rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line dance' suggests the country-and-western style, but the conga is literally danced in one long line.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin party dance where dancers form a single snaking file.

clue.text: Hear cop shot criminal on estate?

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken up, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A policeman is heard to have been shot by a villain on a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges HEARCOP; the question mark flags that the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who illegally hunts game on a landowner's estate is a criminal there.

clue.text: Steps taken with school accepting a second old boy, the Parisian

indicators.note: the school takes in the pair of letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A school's old boy and a Frenchman take steps together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like stairs; it is a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a Latin ballroom dance, a sequence of steps modelled on a bullfight march.

clue.text: Fast train clearly indicated

definitions.meaning: a train that makes few stops and goes quickly
stated plainly and definitely, as in an explicit wish

explanation.surface: A quick rail service was plainly signposted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a speedy train as a noun and, as an adjective, means explicitly stated.

clue.text: Describe spherical object in war game

parts.note: to paint a scene in words is to describe it
a ball is a sphere

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to describe a round thing in a military exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a game simulating combat in which players shoot dye pellets at each other.

clue.text: Motorcycle company opening new store

indicators.note: the company opens a branch within the store, so it goes inside the other piece
new means the letters of the word store are made over in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A motorbike firm launches a new shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the store as SOTER, and 'opening' means the company opens up inside it, not at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A scooter is a light motorcycle with small wheels, a type of motorbike.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed about turn taken off

indicators.note: the embarrassed colour goes about the turn, enclosing it

parts.note: someone who blushes looks red
a move is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A player blushes after a turn was disallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Removed means taken away or off, as a coat is removed or taken off.

clue.text: Remarkable bistro associated with large English city

indicators.note: read as re-markable, so the letters of the word bistro are rearranged

explanation.surface: A notable restaurant is linked with a big city in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkable' is read as re-markable, rearranging the restaurant word as BRISTO; 'large' then belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a large port city in the south-west of England.

clue.text: Fruit bats

definitions.meaning: long curved yellow fruit, in the plural
bats is informal for crazy or mad

explanation.surface: A reference to fruit bats, the flying mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the plural of a tropical fruit and also slang meaning mad, like bats.

clue.text: Good-looking police officer retiring

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a British police rank
retiring means shy and reserved

explanation.surface: A handsome policeman is stepping down from the force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like leaving work; it means bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British slang for attractive, describing an appealing person.

clue.text: Couple in generally OK environment

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: A pair living in surroundings that are mostly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To yoke is to couple, join two things together, as oxen are paired under a yoke.

clue.text: Old soldiers Manet's shown adrift crossing inlet

indicators.note: the scrambled painter's name spans the inlet, holding it within
adrift means out of place, so the letters of Manet's are jumbled

parts.note: an arm of the sea is an inlet

explanation.surface: A Manet painting shows old soldiers drifting across a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown adrift' scrambles the painter's name with its S into MENATS, and 'crossing' has it straddle the inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: In historical usage these were armed soldiers, especially heavily equipped medieval fighters.

clue.text: Gibe involving a daughter of doubtful honesty

indicators.note: the gibe word involves, takes in, the other letters

parts.note: a shy is a throw, and also a jibe or gibe

explanation.surface: A taunt aimed at a daughter accused of dishonesty.
explanation.definitionFit: A shady deal or person is of questionable honesty, possibly crooked.

clue.text: Make neither profit nor loss in holiday flat

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
flat means level or even

explanation.surface: An apartment rented for a holiday merely covers its costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' suggests an apartment; it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that covers exactly its costs comes out with no gain and no deficit.

clue.text: Indefinite number in region's theatre

indicators.note: the number is placed in the region word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: an area is a region; the 's is the possessive
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: An unknown number of people attend the local theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue or setting for performances or contests, a theatre in the broad sense.

clue.text: Conceit, for example, on top of obnoxiousness

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Vanity, for instance, as the peak of obnoxious behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is excessive self-regard, an inflated sense of self.

clue.text: Child's toy failing to start? Current required

indicators.note: the toy's word fails to begin, losing its first letter

parts.note: a teddy bear is a child's toy

explanation.surface: A child's toy won't start because it needs new batteries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like electricity for the toy; it is a swirl of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a small circular current in water or air.

clue.text: Half-hearted, Democrat and Conservative after outcome, both sides having been ousted

indicators.note: the Conservative comes after the outcome in the order of letters
the outcome word loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: a result is an outcome
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician gives a lukewarm reaction after an election result ousts both parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both sides having been ousted' trims RESULT to ESUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Desultory means lacking purpose or enthusiasm, done in an unmethodical, lukewarm way.
